gloss: Inari (deity of rice/prosperity); Inari shrine; inari sushi

definitions.gloss: Inari; deity of rice, harvest, and prosperity
definitions.explanation: A major deity in Shinto, associated with rice, agriculture, fertility, and business success. Foxes serve as Inari's messengers, which is why fox statues are found at Inari shrines.
A shrine dedicated to the Inari deity. Recognizable by their red torii gates and fox statues. There are roughly 30,000 Inari shrines across Japan.

definitions.gloss: inari sushi; sushi rice in a fried tofu pouch
definitions.explanation: Short for いなり{寿司|ずし}. A type of sushi made by stuffing vinegared rice into a pouch of sweetly seasoned fried tofu. Named after the Inari deity because foxes are said to love fried tofu.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Inari is one of the most widely worshipped deities in Japan. {伏見稲荷大社|ふしみいなりたいしゃ} in Kyoto is the head shrine and one of Japan's most visited tourist sites. Inari shrines are easily identified by their ⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧⟦{鳥居|とりい}→鳥居：05956_torii⟧ (red torii gates) and ⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{像|ぞう}→像：03691_zou⟧ (fox statues).

The connection between Inari and fried tofu (⟦{油揚|あぶらあ}げ→油揚げ：07477_aburaage⟧) comes from the belief that foxes love ⟦{油揚|あぶらあ}げ→油揚げ：07477_aburaage⟧, which is why the sushi wrapped in fried tofu is called {稲荷|いなり}ずし.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {稲荷|いなり}⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧ (Inari shrine)
- {稲荷|いなり}ずし (inari sushi)
- お{稲荷|いなり}さん (affectionate term for Inari or inari sushi)
- {伏見稲荷|ふしみいなり} (Fushimi Inari, the most famous Inari shrine)
